meta.title: Dongpirang Mural Village, Tongyeong — Travel Guide & Visitor Info
meta.description: The complete guide to Dongpirang Mural Village (동피랑 벽화마을): a seaside art village in Tongyeong, Gyeongsangnam-do, Korea. Since 2008 a community painting project by residents and artists has turned an ageing fishing hillside into an open-air gallery of murals, stairs and corners. Opening hours, how to get there, accessibility, photo spots and visitor reviews — all in one place.

nonprofitBanner.text: This is an independent, non-profit guide compiled by travel enthusiasts to provide the most objective information about visiting Dongpirang Mural Village. It is free, and we are affiliated with no organization.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.text: So that every traveler who visits Tongyeong does not miss this seaside art village brought back to life by residents and artists, we have gathered scattered official information into this guide — purely to give you the most authentic alleys, art and sea views.

hero.title: Dongpirang Mural Village (동피랑 벽화마을)
hero.subtitle: From an ageing hillside village on the verge of being forgotten, to an open-air gallery facing the sea of Tongyeong. Climb the painted stairs and meet fairy-tale characters, carp, flowers and sea breeze on every wall and every step — a seaside art village revived by residents and artists together.

quickFactsDashboard.title: Dongpirang at a Glance
quickFactsDashboard.subtitle: Key facts gathered in one place for quick reading and fast decisions.

items.label: Art project since
items.note: The 'Dongpirang Art Project' launched by residents and artists of Dongho-dong, Tongyeong, gradually turned the ageing hillside housing area into an open gallery.

items.label: Terrain
items.note: The village rises in tiers up a hillside; the painted stone stairs are its signature — consider the slope if you have a stroller or limited mobility.

items.label: Admission
items.note: Public alleys, free and open long-term, no ticket or reservation — it is a real village where people live.

items.label: Viewpoint
items.note: From the top you overlook Tongyeong's Gangguan Port (강구안) and its islands — one of the most photogenic corners of the village.

hiddenRules.title: Safety Tips for the Alleys & Slopes
hiddenRules.subtitle: The hard part of Dongpirang is not finding the way, but remembering 'this is a real village where people live'. Think about residents, slopes and camera etiquette, and the experience upgrades from 'rushing check-ins' to 'strolling slowly'.

highlights.label: Stairs & slope
highlights.note: Built on a hillside, the painted stairs often have ups and downs; with kids, elders or heavy gear, slow down and rest in stages.

highlights.label: Residents' lives
highlights.note: Behind the walls are homes — keep your voice down, don't shout, and never open private doors or cut through backyards.

highlights.label: Narrow & peak
highlights.note: Popular corners are tiny; tour groups and photo crowds overlap and queue easily — go early or on weekdays for empty shots.

panels.q: Do I have to climb to the very top? Is there an alternative?
panels.a: Not necessarily. The core murals cluster on the middle slope up from Gangguan; those with limited stamina can stroll the middle section slowly and keep the top for the view. The village entrance and Gangguan are flat and easiest to enter.
items: With a stroller or elders, enter gently from the Gangguan side — no need to force the summit.
Some steep sections have handrails and rest platforms for staged climbing.

panels.q: Why avoid residents' lives when photographing?
panels.a: Because Dongpirang is still a lived-in village; behind the walls and doors is residents' daily life. Respecting privacy, lowering your voice and not touching items at doors is what lets it remain a shared open gallery long-term.

panels.q: May I paint on the walls or place props?
panels.a: No. All murals are protected — please do not touch, lean, write or post on them, nor place private props; keeping the walls as they are is basic respect for creators and residents.

complianceGuide.title: Dongpirang · Visitor & Co-living Etiquette
complianceGuide.subtitle: This is both a visitor hotspot and residents' daily home. Following these rules is double respect for people and place.

rules.title: Don't touch or paint the murals
rules.text: All wall paintings are artworks — don't touch, lean, write or post on them; for a better angle, don't cross rails or step on planters.
items: Comply with signs reading 'No painting' or 'Do not touch'.
Use drones only in permitted areas and times to avoid disturbing residents.

rules.title: Take your trash with you
rules.text: Bins in the alleys are limited and the seaside wind scatters litter — bring a small bag and take everything away when you leave.

rules.title: Quiet viewing
rules.text: Many come specifically for the calm walls and sea at dawn and dusk — lower your voice, no loud music, leave the quiet to the walls and the sea.

rules.title: No smoking or open flame
rules.text: With dense wood structures and old houses, the whole area is smoke-free; no open flame to prevent fire reaching homes.

higashiyamaRoute.title: Tongyeong Half-Day Loop: Sea, Hills & Alleys
higashiyamaRoute.subtitle: Not just 'who it suits', but a half-day route you can follow directly. Centered on Dongpirang, it also links Gangguan, the Central Market and the Tongyeong Cable Car.

steps.title: [Start] Gangguan Port (강구안) — boat & overlook
steps.text: Gather supplies and use the restroom at Gangguan, and overlook the hillside where Dongpirang sits — the most stable, best-equipped gateway.
tips: Gangguan is Tongyeong's signature harbor; by day read the terrain and arrange a sea cruise.

steps.title: [Main] Gangguan → climb Dongpirang
steps.text: From the Gangguan side climb the painted stairs, strolling the mural alleys at your pace; save the warm afternoon-to-dusk light for walls and sea.
tips: With a stroller or elders, enter from the gentle side — no need to force the summit.

steps.title: [Extend] Dongpirang top → sea view over Gangguan
steps.text: From the top overlook Gangguan and the islands, then descend gently, linking 'mural — sea — hill town' into one line.

steps.title: [Loop] Jungang Market (중앙시장) food & stroll
steps.text: After descending, head to Tongyeong Central Market for gimbap, seafood and local snacks, joining art with local flavors.

steps.title: [End] Gangguan night view or return
steps.text: If time allows, return to Gangguan at dusk for the harbor night view, or take a bus/taxi back — a complete 'art + harbor + food' half-day package.
tips: If alleys are crowded in peak, have dinner at the Central Market to avoid the rush.

higashiyamaRoute.disclaimer: This route emphasizes a closed loop you can follow as-is; if you only want murals, keep the first two segments and treat the market and cable car as optional add-ons.

intro.title: Getting to Know Dongpirang Mural Village
intro.description: Dongpirang Mural Village (동피랑 벽화마을) sits in Dongho-dong, Tongyeong-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, Korea — an art village facing the sea and rising in tiers up a hillside. '동피랑 (Dongpirang)' combines 'East (동)' with a local term for a steep hillside; it was once just an ageing fishing-residential area near Gangguan. From 2008, residents and artists launched the 'Dongpirang Art Project', painting faded walls, stairs and corners into fairy-tale scenes, turning a 'soon-forgotten slope village' into one of Tongyeong's most recognizable cultural landmarks. Even more, it preserves a narrative few villages display so openly: how art turned a declining old village back into a living room shared by residents and travelers.

visitGuide.title: Visitor Guide
visitGuide.description: Dongpirang is a free, open public alley — no gate, no reservation. The ideal approach is usually not 'wander by day' but to plan backward from light and stamina: resupply and use the restroom at Gangguan first, then give the warm afternoon-to-dusk light to the walls and sea. Facilities are minimal and commercial feel is low — which is exactly its charm.
items: Best is afternoon to dusk: west-facing walls catch the warmest light, and sea with murals frame best.
Best angles cluster on upper stairs and corners, capturing murals, alleys and the Gangguan sea view together.
From Gangguan (강구안) it's a 5–15 min walk uphill to enter the village via painted stairs.
Almost no commercial supply inside; water, restrooms and rest are better at Gangguan or the foot.

alsoKnownAs.title: Highlights
items: A real lived-in village painted by residents and artists, not a made-up theme park
Painted stairs and corners rising up the slope — Tongyeong's most photogenic 'open-air gallery'
From the top, overlook Gangguan Port (강구안) and its islands
Free and open, highly public — a model case of 'art in community'

transportSection.title: Transport & Getting There
transportSection.subtitle: A structured guide to reaching Tongyeong, city transfers, walking/cycling, parking and EV charging for Dongpirang.
transportSection.overviewText: Dongpirang is in Dongho-dong, Tongyeong-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, right next to Tongyeong's signature harbor — Gangguan (강구안). The easiest external link is an express/intercity bus from Seoul, Busan etc. directly to Tongyeong, or a transfer from Gimhae Airport (Busan). In the city, the village is only minutes from Gangguan on foot. Built on a seaside slope, from Gangguan you walk up painted stone stairs about 5–15 minutes to enter.
transportSection.overviewText2: Dongpirang is open alleys with no walls or gates. Plan transport, parking and the climb together — entering from the gentle side greatly reduces the climb, especially with elders, infants or luggage.
arrivalItems: Dongpirang is on the north slope above Gangguan; from Gangguan a 5–15 min walk uphill enters the village.
No large dedicated lot in the village — use Gangguan public parking or nearby paid lots, then walk in.
Weekends and holidays get very crowded; narrow alleys jam — strongly prefer transit or off-peak.

bestTime.title: Best time to arrive
bestTime.text: Dongpirang is visitable any time, but the photo ceiling is set by the afternoon-to-dusk light window. Set your climb about 60 minutes before sunset; if the weather is bad for photos, shift focus to a Gangguan cruise, Central Market food or the Tongyeong Cable Car.

officialManagement.title: About the Village
officialManagement.text: Dongpirang Mural Village is an art village in Dongho-dong, Tongyeong-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, Korea, transformed from an ageing fishing-residential hillside and maintained by Tongyeong City together with local residents and artists as a community art space. Long a place where residents' lives, travelers' photos and sea views coexist, it is also one of Korea's representative cases of 'art in community' and 'local regeneration'.

humanities.title: History & Art Intervention
humanities.subtitle: Following the fishing-village past, the art project and on-site signs, we present the historical context of Dongpirang — why it is more than 'pretty walls'.

sections.title: The name & past: an old slope village by Gangguan
sections.content: '동피랑 (Dongpirang)' combines 'East (동, a direction)' with a local term for a steep hillside, originally referring to an ageing hillside residential area in Dongho-dong, Tongyeong, near Gangguan (강구안). Before becoming a painted village, it was an ordinary fishing corner beside boats and sea breeze; with population outflow and ageing houses, it once faced being forgotten.

sections.title: 2007: a mural contest to 'color the hometown'
sections.content: In the early 2000s the local government planned to demolish this ageing hillside housing area to rebuild the military lookout 'Dongporu Pavilion (Dongporu)', established by Admiral Yi Sun-sin, and turn its surroundings into a park. To keep this living, warm community, in 2007 local citizen groups launched the 'Color Dongpirang — National Mural Contest'. Art students and painters from across the country responded, painting faded walls, stairs, fences and even water tanks with vivid fairy-tale scenes. This community action, where residents actively gave their outer walls to artists, turned art into a way to keep people and memory.

sections.title: Gangguan & Dongporu: the geographic base between sea and hill
sections.content: Dongpirang sits right next to Gangguan (강구안), Tongyeong's signature harbor, and at its highest point stands the rebuilt 'Dongporu Pavilion (Dongporu)' — a viewpoint overlooking the Tongyeong harbor and sunset, whose predecessor was a military lookout established by Admiral Yi Sun-sin in the Joseon era. Long a hub for fishing boats and shipping, Gangguan is now famous for night views, seafood and cruises. Dongpirang, Dongporu and Gangguan, one above the other, together form the visual and culinary center of Tongyeong's 'harbor old town'.

sections.title: Murals, stairs & corners: the language of art design
sections.content: Beyond fairy-tale characters and carp, the most-photographed elements are the painted stone stairs and corner walls rising up the slope. They are both wayfinding and turn 'the climb' into a small exhibition; the negative space between walls and the sea borrowed in views are all low-impact, high-empathy spatial design.

sections.title: Why it is called a 'fairy-tale village'
sections.content: Chinese-speaking visitors often describe Dongpirang as a 'fairy-tale mural village facing the sea'. Its charm is not only that it looks good, but that a declining old village was revived by residents and artists — the color on the walls backs a whole narrative of local identity and community regeneration.

sections.title: From old village to public living room
sections.content: Today Dongpirang has become Tongyeong's shared art living room: people stroll at dawn, sketch in the afternoon, and at dusk it is a theater where photographers and travelers wait for the sea breeze to turn. It moves us not only because it became beautiful, but because Tongyeong kept a hard-to-see old slope village as a public lesson in community regeneration.

didYouKnow.title: Did you know?
didYouKnow.text: Dongpirang's legend is more than 'walls painted nicely'. More importantly, it is an ongoing community experiment: residents gave their outer walls to artists and turned daily alleys into a shared gallery, bringing a declining old village back as one of Tongyeong's most recognizable cultural landmarks.

sitePlaques.title: Reading the On-site Signs
sitePlaques.subtitle: When you visit, what's worth slow reading is often not the check-in board, but the official signs explaining 'why this wall is here'.
sitePlaques.intro: The following readings are based on Tongyeong City's Dongpirang Art Project introduction, Gangguan landscape notes and mural creation guides — translating the on-site information you can see but may not read closely into understandable English.

items.title: Dongpirang Art Project & community regeneration
items.body: Such signs usually give the key timeline: from an ageing slope-housing area near Gangguan, the 2008 resident-artist art project gradually painted it into an open gallery. They remind visitors the color was not 'lucky nature' but the result of local policy, art intervention and resident participation.

items.title: Harbor, islands & sea ecology
items.body: Landscape signs stress Gangguan's status as Tongyeong's representative harbor and remind visitors: half of Dongpirang's beauty is the painted walls, half is the real sea outside. Overlooking islands and returning boats from the top is the village's most underrated experience.

items.title: Stairs, corners & fairy-tale characters
items.body: The guide explains 'how to use the village without disturbing residents'. Painted stairs build the ritual of climbing, corner walls guide flow on safe paths, and fairy-tale characters carry warmth and identity — together the design logic of Dongpirang becomes clear.

gallery.title: Photo Gallery
gallery.subtitle: From painted stairs, fairy-tale corners and carp-flower walls to the sea view over Gangguan — see the visual beauty of Dongpirang Mural Village.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Practical info about Dongpirang Mural Village's facilities, history and visit planning.

items.q: Is there parking, and what are the rates?
items.a: No large dedicated lot in the village, but Gangguan public parking (public rates) and the foot temporary lot are reachable, then walk in. Rates vary by season; they fill fast on weekends/peak, so arrive early or prefer transit.

items.q: Are wheelchairs or strollers allowed in the area?
items.a: The core is a sloped stone-stair village; the classic climb is not friendly to wheelchairs/strollers. But you can enter the middle mural area from the gentle Gangguan side; some platforms and gentle slopes are pushable. Keep the summit goal as a view, not a forced climb.

items.q: Are there restrooms or food at the site?
items.a: The alleys have almost no shops or food; the nearest water and public toilets are at Gangguan and the foot (~5–15 min walk back). Stock up before entering.

items.q: Why is it called 'Dongpirang', and does it relate to the fishing village?
items.a: '동피랑 (Dongpirang)' combines 'East (동, a direction)' with a local term for a steep hillside, originally referring to an ageing slope-housing area in Dongho-dong near Gangguan. Its predecessor was an ordinary fishing corner beside boats and sea breeze — the name and the land together tell a regeneration story from old village to art village.

items.q: What is special about its art and local value?
items.a: Dongpirang is not a made-up theme park but a community action where residents gave their outer walls to artists and turned daily alleys into a shared gallery. Stairs, corners and fairy-tale characters form a low-impact, high-empathy spatial design, and a representative Korean case of 'art in community' and 'local regeneration'.
Dongpirang is open public alleys, free long-term and accessible 24 hours — no gate, no ticket, no reservation (respect residents' routines; avoid loud late nights).

items.q: How long does a visit take?
items.a: A typical slow stroll takes about 1–2 hours (climb plus photo stops); allow half a day if adding Gangguan, the Central Market and the Tongyeong Cable Car.

items.q: Can I still go in bad weather?
items.a: Yes — it is open alleys, visitable in any weather. But slopes are slippery in rain, and visibility drops in typhoons or snow; wear grippy shoes and watch the weather. Avoid the top and seaside stairs in thunderstorms and high wind.

items.q: After visiting, what other attractions are worth it?
items.a: From Dongpirang you can link Gangguan (강구안, cruises & night view), Tongyeong Central Market (local food), the Tongyeong Cable Car (harbor & islands), the Hallyeohaesang National Park and Hansan Island (Admiral Yi Sun-sin history) — a Tongyeong 'art–harbor–food–history' half-day line.

scienceArt.title: Mural Art & Community Regeneration: Walls, Stairs & Sea
scienceArt.subtitle: Dig one layer below the surface 'pretty' and you find what is truly rare here: it is at once an art site, a community design, and an open-air classroom.

scienceMuseum.name: A model of community regeneration
scienceMuseum.role: An art site built on an old village
scienceMuseum.highlight: Dongpirang's hardest part is both visible and invisible. Visible are the fairy-tale walls and carp; invisible is the community mechanism where residents gave their outer walls to artists and turned daily alleys into a shared gallery. Visitors see color; planners see a local regeneration system still running.
points: Core: resident participation, art intervention and local identity relit the old village.
Key: public alleys transformed into low-impact, high-empathy space.
Meaning: it upgrades 'local decline' into an observable community-regeneration model.

artMuseum.name: Fairy-tale murals & harbor imagery
artMuseum.role: A cultural symbol of Tongyeong's regeneration
artMuseum.highlight: The cartoon characters, carp and flowers are not mere backdrops; like the painted stairs and seaside corners, they form Dongpirang's identity system: instantly reading as hillside, sea, and a gentle, restrained art aesthetic. From old village to fairy-tale mural plateau, this contrast makes it one of Tongyeong's most memorable cultural images.
points: Imagery: fairy-tale characters, carp, sea and stairs form strong recognition.
Status: Tongyeong's most photogenic art village.
Narrative: it translates community regeneration into a publicly felt aesthetic experience.

outdoorMuseum.title: Photo & Shooting Guide: Dongpirang Spots
outdoorMuseum.subtitle: As Tongyeong's most recognizable art landmark, a few structured spots and times greatly boost your photos' usefulness and beauty.

items.name: Painted stairs · climb ritual
items.background: Climb in the afternoon to dusk; use the painted stairs as foreground and sky-sea as extension — Dongpirang's classic 'enter-the-village' composition.
points: Use the painted stairs as a lead-in line toward the top and sea.
Crouch low to layer walls and sea for a steadier frame.

items.name: Fairy-tale corner wall
items.background: Fairy-tale characters and carp cluster on middle corners; backlight or sidelight makes characters glow; frontlight captures the whole wall's texture.
points: Side light in the morning gives the softest character texture.
Mind the stairs; don't step into residents' private space for a frame.

items.name: Top sea-view deck
items.background: After sunset the blue moment (20–30 min after) balances sky and sea — the most atmospheric window.
points: Shoot in the blue moment for balanced sky and sea color.
Silhouette the colored wall, leaving a large warm sea view.

items.name: Narrow alley & flower wall
items.background: Look back from the foot at the painted alleys, or include harbor and sea in a wider frame — good for a closing wide shot.
points: Use the alley as a lead-in line toward the sea.
Morning mist gives best layers; small aperture for full panorama.

education.title: Why is it a great sample of community regeneration?
education.subtitle: What Dongpirang teaches best is not 'it became pretty', but how it brought declining land back into public life while keeping the memory of the past.

points.title: Land still used by residents
points.text: Dongpirang is not a 'hide the old village and done' case, but a sample where community participation continuously activates the place and turns it into shared space.
items: Residents gave outer walls to artists and co-maintain.
Governance of public alleys and private space coexists long-term.

points.title: Community ethics written into visitor behavior
points.text: Painted stairs, corner flow and sign systems are not just guides but let every visitor, while using the space, respect residents and place.
items: Visitors are guided to stay on low-impact paths.
Art experience and residents' lives do not sacrifice each other.

points.title: Old-village memory into public aesthetics
points.text: Dongpirang did not erase the fishing-village and old-slope past, but through walls and signs lets the public realize what the land went through while enjoying the art.
items: Story depth and art experience complete in one place.
This is exactly the value a non-profit science site should amplify.

audience.title: Who Finds Resonance Here? (Audience Guide)
audience.subtitle: Different visitors each find their best 'way in'.

items.resonance: Free, open and safe art village; kids see fairy-tale characters and the sea, and climb gently from the easy side.
items.tip: Take the climb up; combine Gangguan lawn and Central Market food — adjust order by stamina.

items.resonance: Afternoon-to-dusk colored walls and sea are Tongyeong's most romantic frames, with high shot rates.
items.tip: Secure the top 60 min before sunset; shoot blue moment for both lights and sky color.

items.resonance: As an art sample of community regeneration, wall creation and resident participation are worth a close look.
items.tip: Avoid the most crowded weekends; choose early morning or weekday afternoon to observe art details.

items.resonance: No need to go far — observe harbor old town and art village right in Tongyeong; also link buses, cable car and local food — the ideal start to understand Tongyeong's urban transition.
items.tip: If you can only pick one Tongyeong art landmark, Dongpirang is the best first stop for the 'community regeneration' theme.

lodging.title: Stay Guide: Near the Village, or Convenient?
lodging.subtitle: Tongyeong is a harbor city 'where sea meets town'. We do not recommend specific hotels, but help you read two lodging patterns to choose what fits you.

options.name: Gangguan / city center
options.highlight: Stay at Gangguan or central Tongyeong and Dongpirang, the Central Market and harbor night view are walkable; the night street seafood and snacks suit travelers best. Best for those focused on 'art roam + harbor old town' with high convenience.
points: To Dongpirang ~5–15 min walk, least effort.
Dining, shopping and nightlife extremely rich.
More choices, usually better value.

options.name: Tongyeong Bay / cable-car area
options.highlight: Stay along Tongyeong Bay by the sea; morning harbor strolls and returning boats, then walk or cable car to Dongpirang. Best for those focused on 'sea, night view, slow travel'.
points: Harbor and bike paths at your door, good for mornings and families.
Quieter than the center, good for rest.
To Dongpirang ~10–20 min walk.

lodging.peak: In Tongyeong's spring/autumn peak and holidays (especially summer, Labour Day and Chuseok), rooms tighten as tourists flood in and prices rise clearly. Book weeks ahead; if booking near a holiday, widen the search to Changwon, Jinju and other areas, then take the bus back.
tips: For night views: prefer Gangguan waterfront, sea views morning and dusk.
For convenience and food: choose Gangguan/center, transit and dining at hand.
Before booking, confirm breakfast, parking and EV chargers (key for drivers).
In peak season and holidays plan ahead to avoid no-room or high prices.

sources.title: Sources & References
sources.intro: This guide compiles official, public information about Dongpirang Mural Village from the government tourism portals and regional authorities listed below. We are an independent, non-profit project affiliated with no organization; visitor figures such as the 4.0 / 7,775 rating are referenced from public Google Maps listings.

weather.title: Live Weather & Best Time to Go
weather.subtitle: Coastal Tongyeong changes fast — check the current conditions and the 7-day outlook before you climb the stairs.
weather.error: Live weather is temporarily unavailable — please check again shortly.
weather.note: Conditions reflect Tongyeong's coastal climate; always confirm before you travel.

thunder.risk: Thunderstorms in the area — don't climb the stairs, go in the sea, or shelter under trees.
thunder.plan: Harbor cruises and the cable car are likely suspended; head to indoor spots instead.

heavyRain.risk: Heavy rain — stay away from gullies and low-lying spots on the slope.
heavyRain.plan: Outdoor wandering isn't advised; cruises and the cable car may stop running.
heavyRain.items: Wear a raincoat (skip the long umbrella — it's windy).

lightRain.outfit: Light rain makes the stone steps slippery — watch your footing.
lightRain.plan: Open-air viewpoints will be less enjoyable; time your photos between showers.

rain60.plan: High chance of rain — bring rain gear, prefer indoor stops, and delay the hill climb and harbor walk if you can.

hot.outfit: It's hot — wear light, breathable clothing and avoid the midday sun.
hot.plan: Keep outdoor time short, especially around noon.
hot.items: Bring sunscreen, plenty of water, and something for heat relief.

uv.outfit: Strong UV by the sea — cover up and use protection.
uv.items: Sunscreen, sunglasses, and a sun hat.

coldDiff.outfit: Big day-night temperature swing — bring a layer you can add or remove.

cold.outfit: Cold temperatures — dress warmly against the wind.
cold.items: A thick jacket and a scarf.

wind56.plan: Breezy — harbor cruises and some open-air rides may be paused.
wind56.items: Hats can blow away; skip the loose long skirt.

wind7.risk: Strong wind — keep away from signs, railing edges, and seaside rocks.

fog.risk: Poor visibility — ferries and flights may be delayed.
fog.plan: Not a good time for sea or hill views; the murals are the draw instead.
fog.items: A mask if the air is hazy.

clear.plan: Clear and calm — great for the outdoor murals and sunrise/sunset over the sea.

cloudy.plan: Soft light is perfect for photos; no harsh sun, good for a long stroll.

facilities.title: Visitor Services & Nearby Facilities
facilities.subtitle: What you'll actually find around the village — listed by type, not by brand. We are a non-profit guide and recommend categories, never specific businesses.
facilities.disclaimer: Neutral guide: we describe facility TYPES and where they cluster (Gangguan harbor, the village foot, Tongyeong city), not individual shops or vendors.

categories.title: Restrooms
categories.text: Public restrooms concentrate around Gangguan Harbor and the village foot; inside the alleys facilities are minimal. Use them before you start climbing.
categories.tip: Plan a restroom stop at Gangguan before the uphill walk.

categories.title: Parking & EV charging
categories.text: There is no large dedicated lot in the village. Public and municipal lots sit around Gangguan and the harbor; some have EV chargers. They fill fast on weekends and holidays.
categories.tip: Park near Gangguan and walk in; arrive early in peak season.

categories.title: Dining
categories.text: The village itself has only a few small eateries. Most restaurants, cafés and seafood spots cluster at Gangguan, the Central Market and the waterfront.
categories.tip: Eat at Gangguan or the market, then stroll up to the murals.

categories.title: Convenience & supermarkets
categories.text: Convenience stores and small supermarkets are found along the roads near Gangguan and in the city center — handy for water, snacks and essentials.
categories.tip: Buy water here; almost nothing is sold inside the alleys.

categories.title: Lodging
categories.text: Stay options range from harbor-front guesthouses to city-center hotels and resort-style stays by the bay. None sit inside the village.
categories.tip: See the Stay section for how to choose by location and convenience.

categories.title: Fuel & charging
categories.text: Fuel stations and additional EV charging are available along the city approach roads and near the express bus terminal — refuel before reaching the narrow old town.
categories.tip: Refuel on the city outskirts; the village roads are not for through-traffic.

categories.title: Drinking water
categories.text: Carry your own water — drinking fountains are scarce inside the painted alleys. Refill at Gangguan or convenience stores.
categories.tip: A reusable bottle saves money and cuts waste.

categories.title: Accessibility
categories.text: The village is a steep hillside of stairs and lanes; step-free access is limited. Strollers and wheelchairs can reach the lower alleys from the gentle side.
categories.tip: Enter from the low (Gangguan) side and keep to the wider lower paths.

seasonalStrategy.title: Seasonal Travel Strategy
seasonalStrategy.subtitle: Tongyeong's coast has four clear seasons. Use this as a planning baseline — figures come from long-term climate normals, not today's forecast.
seasonalStrategy.note: Based on Tongyeong's long-term climate normals (Korea Meteorological Administration reference period). Actual weather varies year to year.

rows.watch: Yellow dust days; pack a mask and light layers

rows.weather: Clear, dry, the most stable skies

Quiet alleys and crisp sea light

itineraries.title: Recommended Itineraries
itineraries.subtitle: Pick by who you are, then by how long you have. All routes link Dongpirang with Gangguan and the Tongyeong waterfront.

groups.title: Families with kids
groups.text: Keep the climb short and the rewards frequent — animals, fairy-tale corners and a sea breeze the children can feel.
items: Start at Gangguan and take the gentle lower stairs
Pause at the painted carp and fairy-tale walls
Reward with ice cream or seafood at the harbor
Skip the steep upper alleys with strollers

groups.title: Photographers & nature
groups.text: Chase the afternoon-to-dusk light when west-facing walls glow and the sea turns gold.
items: Arrive about 60 minutes before sunset
Shoot upper corners for murals plus harbor together
Blue hour after sunset for the calm sea
Combine with the Tongyeong Cable Car for height

groups.title: Low-effort / accessible
groups.text: Enjoy the art without the steep climb — stay on the wider lower paths from the Gangguan side.
items: Enter from the low (Gangguan) side
Stay on the gentle lower alleys
Rest at Gangguan viewpoints
Let a shuttle or taxi cover the uphill part

routes.title: Half-day (about 3–4 h)
routes.text: The essentials: harbor, murals and sea.

steps.t: Arrive at Gangguan, use restrooms and snacks
Climb the lower painted stairs (about 30–45 min)
Photo the fairy-tale corners and harbor view
Return to Gangguan for seafood and a cruise
Morning at Gangguan and the Central Market
Late-afternoon climb of Dongpirang for golden light
Tongyeong Cable Car or a harbor cruise at dusk
Dinner by the waterfront, then night views

responsibility.title: Science & Visitor Responsibility
responsibility.subtitle: Dongpirang is a lived-in village, not a stage set. Small habits keep the art, the residents and the coast healthy.

points.title: Respect residents
points.text: People live behind these walls. Keep voices low, don't enter private yards, and avoid blocking doorways while taking photos.

points.title: Protect the coast & ecology
points.text: The murals frame a real fishing harbor and islands. Don't litter the shore, and leave plants and marine life undisturbed.

points.title: Zero waste
points.text: Carry out what you bring. Use the public bins at Gangguan; the narrow alleys have none.

points.title: Stay on low-impact paths
points.text: The painted stairs and signed lanes are the intended route — wandering off-path erodes slopes and disturbs homes.

points.title: Stay safe on slopes
points.text: Stone stairs get slick after rain or fog. Wear grippy shoes, hold the railings, and keep children close near edges.

responsibility.footnote: As a non-profit guide, we share practical, neutral information so every visitor can enjoy Dongpirang responsibly — we are not affiliated with any business.

stories.title: Stories & Local Lore
stories.subtitle: Beyond the paint: the small narratives that make Dongpirang more than a photo stop.

items.title: The year the walls learned to smile (2008)
items.text: When the slope was quietly ageing and residents were leaving, a community art project invited painters to use the outer walls. Neighbors handed over their facades, and a 'soon-forgotten village' became a shared open-air gallery — proof that a town can redraw its own future.

items.title: Gangguan, the harbor that raised it
items.text: Right below Dongpirang lies Gangguan, Tongyeong's old fishing harbor — once full of returning boats, squid lanterns and night markets. The village's charm is half painted walls, half the living sea you overlook from the top.

items.title: The fairy-tale fish & the carp stair
items.text: Among the most loved motifs are carp, fish and fairy-tale characters climbing the steps. Locals say they were chosen because the sea has always fed this town — the art simply made that story visible on the stairs.
